content:
We have carbon NMR peaks: 161.40, 143.85, 130.30, 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm.

We need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm (aliphatic). Here we have four peaks in that region: 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20. Likely each corresponds to a CH3 carbon. Could any be CH2? CH2 carbons are around 20-50 ppm as well. But typical methyl ~10-30, CH2 ~20-40. Distinguish? Need more info. Could use proton NMR to see number of methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
